title: The life gas ledger
description: What each life class puts into the air and takes out of it, and how much (GEN.891, GEN.857, GEN.858, GEN.859; docs/design/habitability/life-classes.md sections 4 and 6; research: reports/non-oxygen-life-byproducts-2026-10-28.md). Rows are keyed by life class number. Every number carries its source tier (T1 to T9) and tweak level (L0 to L4) next to it. The methane flux of a class is its fuel supply (a share of Earth's, physics/life_supply.py) times the area over Earth's times the flux Earth's supply would give; the air holds the flux times the methane's lifetime, up to a cap, and the carbon comes from the air's own carbon dioxide.

earth_donor_methane_tmol_yr.basis: The methane, Tmol a year, that the anoxygenic communities of an Earth-sized world give when its donor supply is Earth's: photoferrotrophs on 80 Tmol of Fe2+ a year fix 20 Tmol of carbon and the food web returns 0.5 methane per carbon, 10 Tmol (Ozaki et al. 2018, read; 0.37e11 molecules/cm2/s), inside the 9 to 67 Tmol of Kharecha et al. 2005 (read)

earth_h2_tmol_yr.basis: The hydrogen, Tmol a year, an Earth-sized world's hydrogenotrophs have when its hydrogen supply is Earth's: Earth's outgassing of 1.7 to 2.9 Tmol a year (Ozaki et al. 2018, read); four hydrogen make one methane, so the methane is a quarter of it

h2_per_methane.basis: CO2 + 4 H2 -> CH4 + 2 H2O (the stoichiometry of hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis)

methane_per_buried_carbon.basis: 2 CH2O -> CH4 + CO2: the organic carbon that is buried or fermented with no oxidant left ends half as methane (stoichiometry)

methane_lifetime_yr.basis: The life of methane in an air with no free oxygen, years: Kharecha et al. 2005 give 100 ppmv to 3.5 percent of methane for 9 to 67 Tmol a year, which is 2e3 to 9e4 years, and Catling and Zahnle 2020 (read) call it long-lived where hydroxyl is scarce; the geometric middle

methane_max_share.basis: The most methane of an anoxic air, as a share of its molecules: 3.5 percent (Kharecha et al. 2005, read abstract)

carbon_left_share.basis: The share of the air's carbon dioxide that methane-making life leaves in the air: the methane's carbon comes out of it, so it cannot take more than it has

oxygen_max_share.basis: The most free oxygen, as a share of the air's molecules, in which methane builds up: above a part in a thousand hydroxyl and ozone chemistry give methane a life of decades (Earth's, 21 percent oxygen, holds 1.8 ppmv); the methane of a ledger row is not added to an air with more oxygen than this

hydrogen_max_share.basis: The most hydrogen an air holds where hydrogen-eating life lives, as a mole share: at or below 1e-4 (Catling and Zahnle 2020, read; Kharecha et al. 2005)

apply_rise.basis: The air takes new methane only when the target is this much above what it holds, so that applying the ledger again changes nothing (a numerical choice)

1.name: Oxygenic light-eaters
1.note: Before the oxygen rise the food web of the buried organic carbon makes methane and carbon dioxide; at the rise the oxygen burns the methane (physics/biogenic_oxygen.py), so the row gives none after it. Oxygen itself is GEN.855.
1.basis: The byproducts report's table (an anoxic air with oxygenic photosynthesis holds methane until the reductants are spent) and life-classes.md section 4, row 1

2.name: Anoxygenic light-eaters
2.note: Carbon is fixed with H2, Fe2+ or H2S for electrons; the food web makes the methane, donor-limited at 1e-4 to 1e-2 of today's biosphere. Never any oxygen.
2.basis: The byproducts report section 4 (Kharecha et al. 2005; Ozaki et al. 2018; Catling and Zahnle 2020)

3.name: Hydrogen eaters
3.note: A methane source on a world with open hydrogen (small); sealed sub-ice and aquifer worlds show nothing in the air because the supply is the water's contact with the rock. 3b (sulfate) makes sulfide, not methane, and is not modelled: its row gives none.
3.basis: life-classes.md section 4, row 3; the stoichiometry of hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis

4.name: Chemolithotrophs
4.note: Draws H2S down and makes sulfate; the air effect needs a sulfur ledger (not built).

5.name: Acid eaters
5.note: Classes 5 to 9 are the second build of the class system (GEN.888, GEN.894).
5.basis: life-classes.md section 4, rows 5 and 9: speculative chemistry

6.name: Dense-carbon-dioxide hydrogen eaters
6.note: As Class 3, in a supercritical carbon dioxide fluid.
6.basis: life-classes.md section 4, row 6 (a methane source; the water separates from the fluid)

7.name: Cold methane hydrogenators
7.note: Hydrogen and acetylene go down and methane up in an air that is already methane; not built.
7.basis: life-classes.md section 4, row 7: the Titan anomalies are a lead, not a detection

8.name: Ammonia-water hydrogen eaters
8.note: As Class 3 (the net air effect is small).

9.name: Silicon acid eaters
9.basis: life-classes.md section 4, rows 5 and 9: speculative chemistry
